cards.text: It's evening now, and Jesus has died on the cross. Then a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph steps into the scene, and friend, you're going to want to lean in for this one.

cards.question: Joseph, the rich man from Arimathea, was himself a ___ of Jesus.

cards.text: Joseph goes to Pilate, the governor who handed Jesus over to be crucified (Matthew 27:26). And he doesn't come empty-handed. He comes with a request.

cards.question: Joseph from Arimathea stands before Pilate the governor. What does he ask for?
Pilate refuses to give Joseph the body of Jesus.

cards.text: Pilate gives the order, and Joseph takes the body of Jesus.

cards.question: Joseph from Arimathea wraps the body of Jesus in a clean ___ cloth.

cards.text: Then Joseph places the body in a tomb cut into the rock. And friend, this is not just any tomb.

cards.question: Joseph from Arimathea places the body of Jesus in a tomb cut into the rock. Whose tomb is it?

cards.text: Then Joseph rolls a great stone across the entrance and goes away. Friend, some mornings my rolling pin wins the fight, and this man just rolled a GREAT stone.
Joseph is gone, but the tomb isn't alone. Two of the women who followed Jesus from Galilee are sitting there, opposite the tomb (Matthew 27:55).

cards.question: Two women who followed Jesus from Galilee are sitting opposite His tomb. Who are they?

answers.text: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary

cards.text: The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees gather in front of Pilate. That man cannot catch a BREAK.

cards.question: The chief priests and Pharisees tell Pilate they remember something Jesus said while He was alive. What was it?

answers.text: After three days I will rise again
I will come down from the cross
Elijah will come to save Me

cards.text: They call Jesus a deceiver, but look at that, friend: they remembered His promise. So they ask Pilate to give the order that the tomb be secured until the third day.

cards.question: The chief priests and Pharisees want Jesus' tomb secured until the third day. What do they say could happen otherwise?

answers.text: The crowds riot at the tomb

cards.question: Pilate tells the chief priests and Pharisees to make the tomb as secure as they know how.

cards.text: Pilate is every boss who ever said, "Handle it however you want." So off they go to the tomb.

cards.question: At Jesus' tomb, the chief priests and Pharisees secure it by ___ the stone and posting the guard.

cards.text: I seal cookie boxes all day, friend, and never once had to post a guard on one. Hang on to this moment, because this story is NOT over.

findings.problem: The opening card states that Jesus has died on the cross. That fact comes from Matthew 27:50, outside this passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Matthew 27:57.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The blank asks what kind of cloth Joseph used (linen, wool or silk). Card 6 gives nothing the baker can reason from, so the pick is pure luck on a wording detail. This is like the Psalm 23 oil example. The passage already has other discovery questions (cards 2 and 12), so this one should get more setup or be replaced with a question about meaning.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card calls Jesus' words 'His promise.' The text only reports what He 'said', and the speakers here call Him a deceiver. Papa Dorin should call it what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Verse 64's full worry never reaches the baker. No card says the leaders fear the disciples would tell the people He has risen from the dead, or that this 'last deception would be worse than the first.' That is the heart of why they want the tomb secured, and it sets up the next passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 18 cites Matthew 27:65-66, but no card ever tells Pilate's words 'You have a guard' (27:65). Card 19 then asks about 'posting the guard' as if the guard had already been introduced. The setup for card 19 is missing.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
